sentences.text:
The first bail application of application was rejected by this Court vide order dated 28.07.2021,
which is reproduced as below :-
"The hard copy of counter affidavit, which was filed through e-filing, is taken on record.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the first informant and learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

The present bail application has been filed by the applicant in Case Crime No. 461 of 2015, under Sections - 363, 366, 120-B, 376D I.P.C. and Section - 6 of POCSO Act,
Police Station - Gadwar, District -Ballia with the prayer to enlarge him on bail.
It has been argued by learned counsel for the applicant that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It has been submitted that applicant is not named in first information report and that the victim was recovered after one year of incident and that in her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., she has not named the applicant.

Learned counsel submitted that for the first time, the involvement of applicant has been shown on the basis of statement of victim girl, recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C., wherein she has made allegation of gang rape.

It was submitted that the allegations of rape made against applicant are thoroughly false and baseless and that he has been named with ulterior motive as he was doing pairavi in case crime no.477 of 2015, which was lodged by father of co-accused Raju Paswan.
It was submitted that in fact victim girl was in love with co-accused Raju Paswan and that she has gone with him at her own free consent.

Regarding Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.22284 of 2016, which was filed before this Court, learned counsel has submitted that by that time applicant was not named in first informant report and that applicant has not concealed any fact.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.22284 of 2016
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: It was further submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 28.10.2020 having no criminal history and that in case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and cooperate in the trial.

Learned counsel for the first informant and learned A.G.A. have opposed the prayer for bail and argued that applicant is continuously absconding since 2016 and that even the process under Section 82 and 83 Cr.P.C. has been executed against applicant.
It has been further submitted that co-accused Raju Paswan has already been convicted and sentenced in this case but the case against applicant could not proceed as he was continuously absconding.
Other co-accused persons are also absconding.

Learned counsel for informant submitted that applicant has tried to mislead this Court by mentioning in the affidavit that the order dated 21.10.2016 in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.-22284 of 2016, was not passed in respect of the applicant.

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.-22284 of 2016
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: Learned counsel has referred the memo of that writ petition and submitted that applicant was one of the petitioner in that petition but in the affidavit filed along with present bail application, applicant has tried to conceal this fact.

It has also been Subhash Paswan vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154753682/
2 submitted that it is apparent that applicant has full knowledge of this case since 2016,
as he has filed a writ petition before this Court and that even applicant was granted interim relief by order dated 21.10.2016, passed in the above stated writ petition, to the effect that in case, applicant surrenders before the Court below within 30 days,
his prayer for bail shall be considered expeditiously but despite that applicant has not surrendered before the Court below and he has continuously absconded for 4 years.

entities.text: Subhash Paswan vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of accusation,
conduct of applicant, gravity of offence and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, the applicant is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.

Hence, the bail application of applicant Subhash Paswan is hereby rejected."
5.
It is submitted by learned counsel for applicant that victim girl was having an affair with co-accused Raju Paswan and she has gone with him.
Applicant was not named in the first information report.
Applicant was not aware about the filing of charge-sheet against him and thus he could not surrender before the court concerned.
Meanwhile, trial of co-accused Raju Paswan was conducted and he has been convicted by the trial court but in appeal he has been granted bail.
Trial of applicant-accused was separated from co-accused Raju Paswan.

It was submitted that applicant is languishing in jail since 28.10.2020 and thus, he has already undergone the detention of more than four years but no witness has been examined so far and thus, trial of the case would take sufficient long time.
Lastly, it was submitted that applicant has no criminal history and that in case the applicant-accused is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate in trial.

6. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that incident relates to the year 2016 and applicant has surrendered before the court after four years and that there are serious allegations against him.
It was submitted that co-accused Raju Paswan has already been convicted by the trial court.

7. Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, nature of allegations, period of custody and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on the merits, a case for bail is made out.
Hence, the present second bail application is hereby allowed.

8. Let the applicant - Subhash Paswan involved in the aforesaid crime be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two local sureties each of the like amount to the satisfaction of court concerned subject to the following conditions:
i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during trial.
ii) The applicant will not pressurize/intimidate the prosecution witnesses.
iii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
Subhash Paswan vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154753682/
3 iv) The applicant will not try to contact, threat or otherwise influence the complainant or any of the witness of the case.
9. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel the bail of applicant in accordance with law.
